preregistered_criteria_failed.why: dAUC is 0.982 but dXMID is 0.990, so dAUC is not 0.05 above the rest
my ceiling of 0.95 was too low; all four exceed 0.98
preregistered_criteria_failed.honest_note: both criteria were mine and both missed; the data is sharper than either

resolution_of_R90.finding: all four metrics classify the published flag at AUC 0.98-0.99, so at the extreme where the flag lives the four definitions agree
resolution_of_R90.why_R90_flipped: R90 used the top quartile of each metric, which lives in the bulk; the metrics agree at the extreme but diverge in the bulk
resolution_of_R90.implication: the sign flip measures a bulk property, not the decision-relevant extreme

decision_criterion_now_fixed: the dataset's own boolean Synergy call (the extreme), because it is dataset-provided rather than invented here, it matches what a screen actually asks, and all four metrics agree there
consequence: the C45-type comparisons using the boolean criterion remain the decision-relevant ones; R90's quartile analysis becomes a bulk sensitivity analysis that does not overturn the extreme-level result
limits: this is association, not the label's generating rule, which is upstream code not present locally
the metrics are so correlated that the 0.982 versus 0.990 difference should not be read as dXMID being better
only 1,550 positives, so extreme-region estimates are affected by rarity
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
